chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthayfir, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abd al-A'la, the freedman of the family of Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When this verse was revealed: 'O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire,' a man from the Muslims sat weeping and said: 'I have become unable to manage myself, yet I am tasked with managing my family.'
'O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is sufficient for you that you command them to do what you command yourself to do, and forbid them from what you forbid yourself from.'
ai.seo_question: How does the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) define the method of protecting one's family from Hellfire according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet (SAW) addresses the companions' anxiety regarding the weight of the command to protect their families from Hellfire by simplifying the mechanism to consistent personal example. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *al-amr bi-l-ma'ruf* (enjoining good) as a practical, behavioral leadership role rather than an abstract duty, where the head of the household must first embody the virtues they wish to instill. The hadith underscores that effective spiritual guidance within the family unit begins with the integrity of the individual's own practice.
